title: Fixed deposits and recurring deposits
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: A fixed deposit (FD) locks a lump sum with a bank for a chosen period at a fixed interest rate; a recurring deposit (RD) does the same with a fixed monthly amount. Rates are typically higher than a savings account — somewhere around 6–7.5% a year depending on bank and tenor, and senior citizens get a bit more. In India, bank deposits are insured by DICGC up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal plus interest combined). FD interest is fully taxable at your slab rate, and banks deduct TDS if interest crosses a yearly threshold (submit Form 15G/15H if your total income is below the taxable limit). Breaking an FD early usually costs 0.5–1% in penalty. FDs suit short-to-medium goals and the safe part of your portfolio, but after tax their return can barely beat inflation.
summary_hinglish: FD mein ek saath paisa fixed byaj par bank mein lock hota hai, RD mein har mahine fixed amount. Byaj lagbhag 6-7.5%, aur DICGC har bank mein ₹5 lakh tak insure karta hai. FD ka interest tumhare slab ke hisaab se taxable hai, TDS kat sakta hai. Time se pehle todne par penalty lagti hai.
summary_hi: FD में एकमुश्त रकम तय ब्याज पर बैंक में लॉक होती है, RD में हर महीने तय रकम। ब्याज लगभग 6-7.5% होता है और DICGC हर बैंक में ₹5 लाख तक बीमा देता है। FD का ब्याज आपके स्लैब पर कर योग्य है। समय से पहले तोड़ने पर जुर्माना लगता है।
